stories.title: Open-source AI agents power a low-cost campaign against 27 companies
stories.summary: Gambit reconstructed a campaign in which an operator used the Strix, Cairn, and Hermes open-source AI harnesses to probe and attack hundreds of targets, compromising at least 27 organizations between September 10 and 15. The operation included web-shell deployment, privilege escalation, cloud-credential theft, and the exfiltration of more than 600,000 payment-card records from two victims, while the operator’s average spend was only about $25 per completed scan. The episode shows why organizations need controls around autonomous scanning, agent identity, tool permissions, and rapid containment—not just model-level safety filters.
stories.impact: Security teams should treat autonomous offensive agents as a scalable threat multiplier and add runtime authorization, egress controls, and continuous detection around agent tooling.
